title: Fixed Convex Sole and Clamped Blank Sheet Rocking Blotter
description: One newly authored complete empty-ink rocking-blotter-inspired desk tool. A whole thick rectangular wooden-look rocker has a continuously changing convex underside and a flat upper deck. One complete finite-thickness blank ivory sheet follows the entire curved lower surface, turns up both short ends and folds inward beneath a separate whole chamfered upper clamp plate. A full central turned knob includes its own integral short stock rooted through the plate into the wood. The sheet has one coherent closed body, not painted decoration, detached patches or a copied paper texture. Its narrow central lower facet is the finite ground sole while both ends rise above ground. Four whole closed editable meshes, four opaque constant PBR roles, metres native Z up and whole horizontal-bounds-centred ground datum. Every curve, folded profile and proportion is original numeric geometry; no earlier pad, blade, stamp or handle imported. Unlike the flat round baren with a raised twisted band, this is a longitudinal convex sole with end-folded sheet and separate clamp plate; unlike the serrated rocker blade it has no cutting edge, tang or end grip, and unlike the plunger stamp it has no guide frame, open foot or raised platen. One complete model zero scenes. Plain category-inspired art only, no ornament, inscription, brand or measured historical reconstruction. Sheet thickness and small fixed overlaps are visual simplifications, not a detachable fitted assembly. No ink, absorption, blotting result, pressure, actual rocking, rolling range, paper deformation, screw threads, clamping force, hand fit, stability, material performance, manufacture or safety capability made or verified. No rigging, animation or interaction.
